""" RIO WebSocket Microphone Bridge - Setup & Usage Guide =====================================================
OVERVIEW -------- The WebSocket Microphone Bridge connects the browser microphone directly to Python for both speech transcript and voice emotion detection, bypassing the need for system microphone access on the Python backend.
Architecture: Browser (WebSpeechAPI) ─── WebSocket (ws://localhost:8765) ──→ Python ↓ ↓ - Captures transcript ────────────────→ ws_server.py - Streams raw audio ────────────────→ voice_detector.feed_audio_chunk() - Shows listening dot get_latest_transcript()
COMPONENTS ----------
1. rio_web/static/mic_bridge.js (Browser Client) - Uses WebSpeechAPI (webkitSpeechRecognition) for transcript - Captures raw audio via ScriptProcessorNode (AudioContext API) - Sends both via WebSocket to Python - Auto-reconnects every 3 seconds if connection drops - Shows listening status indicator (green pulsing dot)
No npm packages needed - purely native browser APIs!
2. rio_bridge/ws_server.py (Python Server) - asyncio-based WebSocket server on port 8765 - Receives {"type": "transcript", "text": ...} messages - Receives {"type": "audio", "data": <base64>} messages - Stores transcripts in thread-safe queue - Feeds audio chunks to voice_detector for emotion analysis
Exposed functions: - get_latest_transcript() → str | None - start_ws_server(host="localhost", port=8765, daemon=True) → Thread
3. perception/voice_detector.py (Enhanced) - New method: feed_audio_chunk(audio_int16, sample_rate) - Processes acoustic emotion from raw audio without needing system mic - Integrates seamlessly with existing emotion pipeline
4. main.py (Updated) - Imports get_latest_transcript, start_ws_server from ws_server - Calls start_ws_server() before main loop - Uses get_latest_transcript() instead of system mic fallback
INSTALLATION ------------
1. Install websockets package: pip install websockets>=12.0
(Already added to requirements.txt)
2. Check rio_web/index.html loads mic_bridge.js: <script src="/static/mic_bridge.js"></script>
(Already added)
STARTUP SEQUENCE ----------------
When you run: python main.py
1. Node.js emotional engine starts (index.js on port 5000) 2. Perception loop starts (face detection, etc.) 3. WebSocket server starts on ws://localhost:8765 4. Browser connects to ws://localhost:8765 automatically 5. Listening indicator appears (green dot with pulse animation) 6. Main loop polls get_latest_transcript() every 2 seconds
BROWSER MICROPHONE SETUP ------------------------
When user opens http://localhost:8000 (rio_web):
1. Browser requests microphone permission 2. mic_bridge.js initializes: - WebSpeechAPI starts continuous listening - AudioContext captures raw 16-bit PCM audio 3. Connection indicator shows status: - Green + PULSE = Actively listening - ✅ Blue = Connected but not currently detecting speech - Orange = Reconnecting - ❌ Red = Error or mic denied
AUDIO FLOW ----------
1. Browser Audio Input ↓ 2. WebSpeechAPI Recognition ├→ Generates final_transcript (text) └→ Sends to ws_server: {"type": "transcript", "text": "hello"} ↓ 3. Browser AudioContext ├→ Captures 16-bit PCM chunks (4096 samples) └→ Sends to ws_server: {"type": "audio", "data": "<base64>", "sample_rate": 48000} ↓ 4. Python ws_server.py receives ├→ Transcript: Adds to transcript_queue └→ Audio: Decodes base64 → calls voice_detector.feed_audio_chunk() ↓ 5. voice_detector.py processes ├→ Extracts acoustic features (pitch, loudness, energy) └→ Generates EmotionVector (confidence, emotions: joy/sadness/fear/etc.) ↓ 6. main.py ├→ Calls get_latest_transcript() → user text ├→ Gets latest EmotionVector from voice_detector └→ Runs pipeline: transcript + emotion → response
TROUBLESHOOTING ---------------
Issue: "WebSocket connection refused" Solution: - Ensure main.py is running - Check ws_server is starting (look for log: "[WS] Server thread started") - Check port 8765 is not in use: netstat -ano | findstr :8765
Issue: "Microphone denied" (red dot in browser) Solution: - Check browser privacy settings - Allow microphone access for localhost - For Chrome: Settings → Privacy → Site Settings → Microphone → Allow localhost - Refresh the page and click "Allow" when prompted
Issue: "WebSpeechAPI not supported in this browser" Solution: - Use Chrome, Edge, or Safari - Firefox has limited WebSpeechAPI support - mic_bridge.js will log warning but still capture raw audio
Issue: "No transcript received in Python" Solution: - Check browser console (F12) for mic_bridge.js logs - Verify WebSocket connection (look for "Client X connected" in server logs) - Ensure you speak clearly and pause between sentences - WebSpeechAPI requires ~5 seconds of silence to finalize transcript
DEBUG MODE ----------
To test ws_server.py directly without main.py:
python -m rio_bridge.ws_server
This will start the WebSocket server and print received transcripts:
[WS] WebSocket server listening on ws://localhost:8765 Received: hello there Received: how are you
SPEECH BEHAVIOR ---------------
WebSpeechAPI triggers final_transcript when: - User pauses for ~0.5-1 second - Maximum phrase reached (usually ~10 seconds) - Browser detects speech end
RIO main loop: - Checks for transcript every 2 seconds - Only runs pipeline if transcript is non-empty - Prints "[RIO] Waiting for user input..." if no transcript
TESTING CHECKLIST -----------------
✅ mic_bridge.js loads (check browser console) ✅ WebSocket connects (green dot appears) ✅ Speak into mic, see transcript in console ✅ get_latest_transcript() returns text ✅ voice_detector.feed_audio_chunk() processes audio ✅ EmotionVector generated with confidence ✅ main.py receives transcript and runs pipeline ✅ RIO speaks response and updates face
PERFORMANCE NOTES -----------------
- WebSocket audio chunks: ~4KB per 4096 samples (base64 encoded) - Frequency: ~10-12 chunks per second @ 48kHz - Total bandwidth: ~40-50 KB/s (negligible for localhost) - No network issues on single machine - All processing happens locally, no cloud API calls
SECURITY NOTES ---------------
- WebSocket only listens on localhost:8765 (not exposed to network) - Transcripts and audio stay within local network - No data sent to external services - Browser microphone access requires explicit user consent
FUTURE ENHANCEMENTS -------------------
- Support multi-language transcription (currently en-US) - Add noise cancellation via browser APIs - Implement voice activity detection (VAD) - Stream continuous transcription instead of final results - Add audio playback feedback - Support Web Audio API insights (frequency analysis, etc.) """

import time import logging import threading from collections import deque
from config import ( PERCEPTION_LOOP_INTERVAL, DETECTOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, WEBCAM_INDEX, SHORT_TERM_MEMORY_SIZE, ) from perception.emotion_fusion import EmotionFusionEngine, EmotionVector
logger = logging.getLogger("PerceptionLoop")

Thread safety: get_fused() / get_stimulus() / get_transcript() are safe to call from any thread — they acquire a short lock and return copies. """

# Short-term memory: deque of recent StimulusObjects (max 7) self._stimulus_history: deque[dict] = deque(maxlen=SHORT_TERM_MEMORY_SIZE)

# Detector instances (lazy-init inside thread to avoid camera conflict) self._face_detector = None self._posture_detector = None self._voice_detector = None
# Shared camera frame (face and posture share one camera capture) self._shared_frame = None
# Loop diagnostics self._loop_count = 0 self._last_loop_ts = 0.0

def _init_detectors(self): """Initialise detectors inside the loop thread to avoid cross-thread issues.""" if self.enable_face: try: from perception.face_detector import FaceEmotionDetector self._face_detector = FaceEmotionDetector(camera_index=self.camera_index) logger.info("FaceEmotionDetector initialised.") except Exception as e: logger.warning(f"FaceEmotionDetector unavailable: {e}")

def _loop(self): """ Core perception loop — runs at ~10fps in a daemon thread.

Write results behind lock for safe consumption by LangGraph """ logger.info("Perception loop started.") self._init_detectors() self._ready_event.set() logger.info("PerceptionLoop ready — all detectors initialised.")
while not self._stop_event.is_set(): t_start = time.perf_counter()
# ── 1. Capture shared camera frame ────────────────────────── frame = None if self._face_detector: frame = self._face_detector.get_frame() self._shared_frame = frame
# ── 2. Face detection ──────────────────────────────────────── if self._face_detector and frame is not None: try: face_vector = self._face_detector.detect(frame=frame) if face_vector.confidence >= DETECTOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: self._fusion.update("face", face_vector) except Exception as e: logger.debug(f"Face detect error: {e}")

Posture detection (same frame) ──────────────────────── if self._posture_detector and frame is not None: try: posture_vector = self._posture_detector.detect(frame=frame) if posture_vector.confidence >= DETECTOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: self._fusion.update("posture", posture_vector) except Exception as e: logger.debug(f"Posture detect error: {e}")
# ── 4. Voice (non-blocking poll) ───────────────────────────── if self._voice_detector: try: voice_vector = self._voice_detector.get_latest() transcript = self._voice_detector.get_transcript() if voice_vector.confidence >= DETECTOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: self._fusion.update("voice", voice_vector) except Exception as e: logger.debug(f"Voice poll error: {e}") else: transcript = ""

# ── 6. Build StimulusObject ────────────────────────────────── stimulus_obj = self._fusion.build_stimulus( fused, label="user_emotional_state" )
# ── 7. self._loop_count += 1 self._last_loop_ts = time.time()
# ── 8. Sleep to maintain target fps ───────────────────────── elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t_start sleep_for = max(0.0, self.loop_interval - elapsed) self._stop_event.wait(timeout=sleep_for)
self._release_detectors() logger.info(f"Perception loop stopped after {self._loop_count} cycles.")

def get_fused(self) -> EmotionVector: """ Return the latest smoothed fused EmotionVector. Thread-safe — call from LangGraph nodes freely. """ with self._lock: return self._latest_fused
